title: Step for Step - Subareas of mobility-related activities in older people and consequences for physiotherapeutic assessments
summary:
Maintaining mobility in older age is an important topic in physiotherapy. Several factors, e.g. fall risk or decline of walking ability or strength, are contributing to a loss of mobility and therefore should be detected as soon as possible. In physiotherapy, several instruments for detecting mobility decline are available.
Two important instruments are the Timed Up and Go Test (TUG) and the measurement of stair climbing speed. 
The aim of this study is to evaluate these instruments using measurement technologies such as force plates and body sensors, to gain deeper insights on partial components of these instruments.
conditions: Mobility during daily living situations and stair climbing.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- age of 18 - 29 years (group 1) or 65+ years (group b)
- able to walk for 200 meters
- walking ability of 60 meters without the use of walking aids
- ability to negotiate a flight of stairs (13 steps, regardless of negotiation strategy)
Exclusion criteria:
- body weight >150kg
- balance disturbances that can disturb the ability to walk
- congenital or acquired changes of the musculoskeletal system that is accompanied by relevant changes in gait, including lower extremity prothesis 
- Pain that leads to changes in gait and stance ability
- neurologic diseases or lowered sensitivity at the extremities
- Wounds or acute inflammation on body regions where inertial sensors are placed
- acute injuries
- eye diseases with an impaired eyesight that cannot be corrected
- surgeries at any extremities in the last 12 months
- limited ability to follow the instructions (e.g. cognitive impairment, hearing impairment, insufficient ability to understand German)
